::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Decr 19th [1865]  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS British Library Add MSS 54920: 126-7
:::

Dear [Mr Macmillan](people/person_939.qmd),
I shall be very glad to mark off the chapters that would suit best for the school abridgement of [Golden Deeds](cmy_books/cmybook_51.qmd). Having tried some on my own school children I can do it the better. I should fancy the reading book [Mr Lea](people/person_853.qmd) proposes to be something of what [Dr Vaughan](people/person_1439.qmd) was about, and I also know a lady who I believe has one in hand.

Tell me how soon you would like to have a selection made, and also how many chapters would suit your purposes. I don’t think one could find <u>many</u> very striking money Golden Deeds. Perhaps Mr Budgett’s throwing all his adulterated pepper and sugar into the Bristol Channel is the best on record.[^1] There is a curious story in [Lady Pomfret’s letters](other_books/otherbook_439.qmd) of a man who made restitution of Church Property. I looked it out for the Golden Deeds but the motives would not have been enough understood.

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

Many thanks for Mr Lea’s pamphlet. I am just going to read it, I have not heard of Meltrai for a long time.

---

[^1]: Samuel Budgett (1794–1851), the subject of the bestselling biography by William Arthur, *The Successful Merchant* (London 1852).
